t.E413.agn: In 2017 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern at the reported uses. EFSA noted that some cases of hypersensitivity (allergy) linked to tragacanth have been reported and that these may be due to proteins in the gum.
t.E413.body: Tragacanth is not absorbed intact in the gut and is partly fermented by gut bacteria.
t.E413.eff.0.t: Some cases of hypersensitivity (allergy) have been reported; these may be due to proteins in the gum
t.E413.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E413.prod: Obtained by physical means from plant seeds or tree exudate (gum).
t.E413.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed. Some cases of hypersensitivity have been reported.
t.E413.regx.1: Group I additive; may not be used in jelly mini-cups.
t.E413.summary: A natural gum (tragacanth) that exudes from the stem of the Astragalus plant. It thickens confectionery and sauces.
